👂 Did you know that abnormal bone remodelling inside the ear can interfere with hearing?
Episode:20
Otosclerosis is a condition in which abnormal bone remodelling can affect the stapes, one of the three tiny bones in the middle ear.
🦴 What happens? The stapes normally helps transmit sound vibrations to the inner ear. When it becomes fixed or less mobile, sound transmission can be reduced.
🔊 What are the symptoms? Hearing loss often develops gradually and may affect one or both ears. Some people also experience tinnitus.

niche.title: 8 Cranial Bones Mnemonic: Old People From Texas Eat Spiders | Skull Anatomy #shorts
niche.description:
Can you name all 8 cranial bones? One silly sentence does it: Old People From Texas Eat Spiders 🦴

O → Occipital: the back of your skull (the spinal cord exits through its foramen magnum)
P → Parietal: top and sides (a pair)
F → Frontal: your forehead
T → Temporal: right above your ears (a pair)
E → Ethmoid: tucked between your eye sockets
S → Sphenoid: the "keystone" that joins almost every other skull bone
6 names, but parietal and temporal come in pairs = 8 cranial bones.

Quick test: your spinal cord leaves the skull through which bone? Answer in the video.

niche.description:
Can you name all 7 bones of the eye socket? Remember: Many Friendly Zebras Enjoy Lazy Summer Picnics 🦓

Maxilla, Frontal, Zygomatic, Ethmoid, Lacrimal, Sphenoid, Palatine.
Lateral wall = zygomatic + greater wing of sphenoid (the strongest wall).
Medial wall = ethmoid (its paper-thin orbital plate, the lamina papyracea) + lacrimal, maxilla, sphenoid: the thinnest wall.
Roof = frontal + lesser wing of sphenoid. Floor = maxilla, zygomatic, palatine.

niche.description:
虫 chóng (chong): insect, worm, bug. Kangxi radical 142.

How do you say "insect" in Chinese? 虫.

The oracle-bone graph drew a coiled snake, head and curled body clearly visible, and it was read huǐ. 虫 originally covered all creeping things: snakes, worms, insects, lizards. It is now one of the most productive semantic radicals in the language, covering insects, reptiles, molluscs, parasites and amphibians. In everyday speech 虫子 chóngzi is the word for a bug, while 昆虫 kūnchóng is the more formal term for insect.
